title: fix(gateway): session lists and health fail after a plugin reload retires an agent's plugin registry
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions.list`, `sessions.catalog.list`, `sessions.describe`, `sessions.resolve`, and `health` fail with `PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin <provider> was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.` after a plugin reload retires an agent's private plugin registry while a model-runtime replacement is pending.

## User Impact

Session lists and health keep working when an agent's prepared plugin registry retires during a plugin reload. Session rows show thinking levels from the active Gateway policy until the replacement catalog is published, then use the replacement's policy. Runs keep their exact captured thinking policy across a stale mark as long as the registry that supplied it is live.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared model catalog rows carry a thinking-policy callback captured from the provider plugin of the prepared runtime's plugin registry. While a model-runtime replacement is pending, the session-row projection keeps serving the previous catalog on purpose so session lists do not stall (#156339). When an agent's workspace differs from the Gateway's, that registry is a private load. A plugin reload can retire it before the replacement exists. Every row read then called the retired instance and threw.

The captured policy now records the `PluginRegistry` that supplied it, and `resolveEffectiveThinkingProfile` checks `isPluginRegistryRetired` before calling it. Registry retirement is recorded in `closePluginRegistryAdmissions` before any instance quiesces, so the check is in place from the first moment the callback would throw. A retired policy falls back to the active registry's provider hook, then to the provider's public policy surface. Catalog data stays available during the replacement. Stale-marking a prepared runtime does not retire its registry, so in-flight runs keep their captured policy.

## Evidence

- Regression: `does not execute a retired prepared thinking policy while adopting its replacement` (`src/gateway/session-row-projection-catalog.test.ts`) publishes a catalog, starts a pending replacement, disposes the policy's registry through `disposePluginRegistryInstances`, reads rows during and after disposal, then adopts the successor's policy. Against the `main` versions of `provider-thinking.ts` and `provider-thinking-catalog.ts` it fails with `PluginInstanceUnavailableError`; with this change it passes.
- Regression: `retains exact thinking policy across a stale mark (borrowed Gateway registry=%s)` (`src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.auth-recovery.test.ts`) proves a stale-marked but live registry keeps its exact policy, for both private and Gateway-borrowed registries.
- Focused runs: `session-row-projection-catalog`, `prepared-model-runtime.auth-recovery`, `model-thinking-default`, `session-utils-model.thinking-default`: 62 tests pass. The other 8 updated test files plus the `prepared-model-runtime` catalog-publication, configured-catalog, and catalog-owner suites also pass.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): `session-row-projection-catalog.test.ts` 12.10s wall (226 ms test execution); `prepared-model-runtime.auth-recovery.test.ts` 16.33s wall (new cases 64 ms combined).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: production typecheck and lint pass. The core-test graph stops on an inherited `main` error in the unchanged `ui/src/components/session-group-defaults-dialog.ts` (`readMissingScopeError` is not imported).
- Autoreview (Codex) reported no findings.
